# core/aes.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/aes.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The AES-128 and AES-256 block ciphers (FIPS 197),
encryption only, which is all that GCM needs.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and a key
schedule is 176 bytes (AES-128) or 240 (AES-256), an encrypted block 16. Not proved: that the output
is AES's (the tests check FIPS 197's vectors and blocks made by OpenSSL),
or that the code is constant time: the S-box is looked up by index, so a
program that shares a machine with an attacker who can time cache misses
leaks key bytes. The S-box is computed when the key is set up, not stored.

`import "core/aes.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`aes128_new`](#aes128_new) | The expanded key of the 16-byte `key` (AES-128). |
| [`aes256_new`](#aes256_new) | The expanded key of the 32-byte `key` (AES-256). |
| [`aes_free`](#aes_free) | Frees an expanded key. |
| [`aes_encrypt`](#aes_encrypt) | AES (128 or 256, as the key was expanded) of one 16-byte block. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `Aes`

```bastio
struct Aes { sbox: Bytes, rk: Bytes, nr: u64 }
```

An expanded key: the S-box (256 bytes), the number of rounds `nr` (10 for
AES-128, 14 for AES-256) and the `nr + 1` round keys (176 or 240 bytes).

## Functions

### `aes128_new`

```bastio
fn aes128_new(key: &Bytes) -> Aes
  requires blen(key) == 16
  ensures aes_ok(result) && result.nr == 10
```

The expanded key of the 16-byte `key` (AES-128).

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(16);
let a = aes128_new(key);
let out = aes_encrypt(a, key);
let first = bget(out, 0);
bfree(out);
aes_free(a);
bfree(key);
// AES-128 of the zero block under the zero key starts 66 e9 4b d4.
if first != 102 { return 1; }
```

### `aes256_new`

```bastio
fn aes256_new(key: &Bytes) -> Aes
  requires blen(key) == 32
  ensures aes_ok(result) && result.nr == 14
```

The expanded key of the 32-byte `key` (AES-256).

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(32);
let a = aes256_new(key);
let block = balloc(16);
let out = aes_encrypt(a, block);
let first = bget(out, 0);
bfree(out);
bfree(block);
aes_free(a);
bfree(key);
// AES-256 of the zero block under the zero key starts dc 95 c0 78.
if first != 220 { return 1; }
```

### `aes_free`

```bastio
fn aes_free(a: Aes)
```

Frees an expanded key.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(16);
let a = aes128_new(key);
aes_free(a);
bfree(key);
```

### `aes_encrypt`

```bastio
fn aes_encrypt(a: &Aes, block: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires aes_ok(a) && blen(block) == 16
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

AES (128 or 256, as the key was expanded) of one 16-byte block.

Example:

```bastio
let mut key = balloc(16);
let mut block = balloc(16);
let mut i = 0;
while i < 16 {
  bset(&mut key, i, cast[u8](i));
  bset(&mut block, i, cast[u8](17 * i));
  i = i + 1;
}
let a = aes128_new(key);
let out = aes_encrypt(a, block);
// FIPS 197 appendix C.1 starts 69 c4 e0 d8 and ends 70 b4 c5 5a.
let ok = bget(out, 0) == 105 && bget(out, 1) == 196 && bget(out, 15) == 90;
bfree(out);
aes_free(a);
bfree(block);
bfree(key);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `aes_ok`

```bastio
spec fn aes_ok(a: &Aes) -> bool {
  blen(a.sbox) == 256 && ((a.nr == 10 && blen(a.rk) == 176) || (a.nr == 14 && blen(a.rk) == 240))
}
```

## Internals

### `aes_xtime`

```bastio
fn aes_xtime(x: u64) -> u64
  requires x < 256
  ensures result < 256
```

Internal: `x` times 2 in GF(2^8) (the AES polynomial).

### `aes_rotl8`

```bastio
fn aes_rotl8(x: u64, n: u64) -> u64
  requires x < 256 && n >= 1 && n <= 7
  ensures result < 256
```

Internal: `x` rotated left by `n` bits as a byte, `n` from 1 to 7.

### `aes_make_sbox`

```bastio
fn aes_make_sbox() -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 256
```

Internal: the S-box, made from the multiplicative inverse in GF(2^8) and
the affine map of FIPS 197, by walking the powers of 3.

### `aes_expand`

```bastio
fn aes_expand(key: &Bytes, nk: u64) -> Aes
  requires (nk == 4 || nk == 8) && blen(key) == 4 * nk
  ensures aes_ok(result) && result.nr == nk + 6
```

Internal: the expanded key of the `4 * nk` bytes of `key`, `nk` 4 (AES-128)
or 8 (AES-256).

### `aes_add_round_key`

```bastio
fn aes_add_round_key(s: &mut Bytes, rk: &Bytes, r: u64)
  requires blen(s) == 16 && r <= 14 && 16 * r + 16 <= blen(rk)
  ensures blen(s) == 16
```

Internal: xors round key `r` (0 to 14, within the key schedule) into the
16-byte state `s`.

### `aes_sub_shift`

```bastio
fn aes_sub_shift(s: &Bytes, sbox: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(s) == 16 && blen(sbox) == 256
  ensures blen(result) == 16
```

Internal: SubBytes then ShiftRows: byte `r` of column `c` of the result is
the substituted byte `r` of column `c + r` (mod 4) of `s`.

### `aes_mix_columns`

```bastio
fn aes_mix_columns(s: &mut Bytes)
  requires blen(s) == 16
  ensures blen(s) == 16
```

Internal: MixColumns in place on the 16-byte `s`.
